newsitem.title: USA: Runaway bus crashes after U.S. interstate chase.
newsitem.headline: Runaway bus crashes after U.S. interstate chase.

text.p: Dozens of police cars pursued a stolen Baltimore city mass transit bus for nearly three hours before the bus finally crashed into a guard rail about 50 miles south of Washington early Wednesday, police said.
Local television stations reported the bus had come to a halt after swerving on Interstate 95, near Occoquan, Va., shutting southbound lanes of the highway, a major East Coast artery.
"The bus is overturned. The suspect is in custody," a Virginia state police spokeswoman said.

A white man, dressed in what appeared to be a bed sheet, allegedly stole the empty bus from the Baltimore municipal lot late Tuesday, and police began pursuing it around 10 P.M. EST as it headed southbound on I-95 toward Washington, said Maryland State Police spokesman Roy Younger.
Younger said the suspect then led police on a chase about 40 miles to the nation's capital, around the city's beltway and south through the Virginia suburb of Alexandria.
Shortly before midnight EST, the bus zipped through the District of Columbia before continuing toward Richmond, Va.
Local television stations reported that up to 50 police cars were in hot pursuit of the stolen bus, some running out of gas and having to abandon the chase.

"He looked like Charles Manson and it looked like he was wearing a bed sheet," Younger told Reuters, likening the suspect to the self-styled cult leader convicted of several murders in California in the 1970s.
"He looked like he was enjoying himself. He was grinning," he said.
The bus was pursued at various times by state troopers from Maryland and Virginia and police officials in the cities of Baltimore, Md., Alexandria, Va., and the District.
